html:
SMTO-EXE-0003 — SMTO needs to check an earlier step before going further

GUID: b00a664b-ab47-432f-8e24-c02f022705a5
Slug: mutation-verification-required
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • An earlier step in this task was interrupted while it was changing something, so SMTO doesn't know if it finished. SMTO won't make more changes, or say the task is done, until that's checked.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In this conversation, ask SMTO to check whether the earlier interrupted step took effect, using only actions that look and don't change anything. Once SMTO can show what happened, it is allowed to carry on.
  2. If you can, look at the affected thing yourself, such as the file, folder, service or website, and tell SMTO what you see. Your own check can confirm the result faster than guessing.
  3. Don't ask SMTO to simply repeat the interrupted step with more time. If the first attempt already worked, repeating it could make the change twice.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports what the interrupted step did and the task continues or finishes normally.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before asking for it again. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't turn off SMTO's safety check for interrupted changes to get past this; it stops changes from being made twice.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The mutation-reconciliation guard blocked a new effectful operation, or a completion claim, because an earlier operation in this task was interrupted (timed out, cancelled or outcome unknown) and its effects are unresolved.

What this means

  • The mutation-reconciliation guard found interrupted operations with unresolved effects while a new external effectful operation or completion claim was being considered. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • The mutation-reconciliation guard found interrupted operations with unresolved effects while a new external effectful operation or completion claim was being considered.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained interrupted operation and its resource effects; a read-only observation must actually establish relevant state to reconcile it.

How to fix it

  • Inspect and reconcile the recorded uncertain operation before further mutation or a completion claim: check the interrupted operation and its target with clearly read-only tools and record what actually happened. Do not blindly re-run the interrupted mutation with a larger timeout, and do not disable the Require mutation reconciliation agent check to bypass this.
  • Inspect and reconcile the recorded uncertain operation before further mutation or a completion claim.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The prior effects are reconciled by supported evidence and the guard permits the next justified action.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
